commands.breakpoint_diff: Show the outline's differences between the breakpoints
commands.check: Check the outline of every view
commands.reading_order: Show the reading order of every view

findings.focus-order-jump: The focus jumps back from {from} to {to}, against the visible order (WCAG 2.4.3).
findings.form-label-missing: The form field {name} has no label.
findings.h1-missing: The page has no h1 heading.
findings.heading-differs: The heading "{text}" shows in {shown} but not in {missing}.
findings.heading-first-not-h1: The first heading is an {level}, "{text}"; the h1 comes later.
findings.heading-image-no-alt: This {level} heading holds only an image without an alt attribute.
findings.heading-skip: The headings jump from {from} to {to} at "{text}".
findings.heading-too-long: This heading is {length, plural, one {# character} other {# characters}} long, more than {max}: "{text}".
findings.img-alt-missing: The image {src} has no alt attribute.
findings.interactive-differs: The {text} shows in {shown} but not in {missing}.
findings.landmark-banner-nested: This banner lies inside a {outer} landmark.
findings.landmark-contentinfo-nested: This contentinfo lies inside a {outer} landmark.
findings.landmark-differs: The landmark {text} shows in {shown} but not in {missing}.
findings.landmark-main-missing: The page has no main landmark.
findings.landmark-unique: {count} {role} landmarks are not told apart by their names; give each its own.
findings.link-empty: The link to {href} has no text.
findings.multiple-h1: The page has {count} h1 headings; another one is "{text}".
findings.reading-order: The {to} comes first on the screen but after the {from} in the source, which screen readers and the keyboard follow (WCAG 1.3.2).

panel.checked: Checked {done} of {total, plural, one {# link} other {# links}}.
panel.cut: Showing the first entries only; MCP outline_get lists them all.
panel.findings: {count, plural, one {# finding} other {# findings}} in this section.
panel.marked: Marked in {count} of {views, plural, one {# view} other {# views}}.
panel.noDifferences: Every view shows the same elements.
panel.orderGood: The reading order follows the source in every view.

rules.focus-order-jump: Focus order jumps against the visible order
rules.heading-image-no-alt: Heading of an image without alt
rules.interactive-differs: Interactive element missing at this breakpoint
rules.landmark-unique: Landmarks not told apart by a name
rules.reading-order: Reading order against the source order

customSelectors.description: Your own selectors, such as [data-cms-block]: the outline lists their matches in every view.
customSelectors.help: Your own selectors the outline lists in every view, with a label. Example: label CMS block, selector [data-cms-block].
customSelectors.label: Custom selectors

elements.description: The elements compared across the breakpoints: shown in one view but missing or hidden in another.
elements.help: The kinds of element the outline compares across the breakpoints - interactive elements, headings and landmarks - and reports where one view shows them and another lacks or hides them. Clear all to compare nothing.
elements.label: Compare across breakpoints

headingMaxLength.description: A heading longer than this many characters is a finding (20 to 1000).
headingMaxLength.help: A heading longer than this many characters is reported as very long; the rule itself is switched in Checks › Findings. Example: 120.
headingMaxLength.label: Longest heading

enabled.description: Request the links of the current page to find broken ones.
enabled.help: Requests the links of the current page to find broken ones and shows them in the outline. When off, it lists the links without checking them.
enabled.label: Check links

rps.description: At most this many link requests a second (1 to 4).
rps.help: At most this many link requests per second (1 to 4), so a link check does not hammer the server.
rps.label: Link requests a second

timeoutMs.description: No further link is requested once one check has run this long, in milliseconds.
timeoutMs.help: No further link is requested once one check has run this long, in milliseconds; the rest stay unchecked. Example: 30000.
timeoutMs.label: Link check time limit

tolerancePx.description: Boxes overlapping by up to this many CSS px still count as one before the other in the reading order (0 to 50).
tolerancePx.help: How many CSS px two neighbouring elements may overlap and still count as one before the other when the reading order is compared with the source. Example: 4.
tolerancePx.label: Reading order tolerance

tools.breakpoint_diff: The differences of the outline between the breakpoints: per page, a row for each heading, landmark or interactive element some views show and others lack or hide, with the views showing it (shown) and missing it (missing) and a cell per view that has it; the findings interactive-differs, heading-differs and landmark-differs. target names the views asked about, each compared with every view on its page; elements narrows the kinds (default outline.diff.elements).
tools.check_links: Checks the links of the current page in the views for broken ones (HEAD, then GET; redirects followed; at most outline.linkCheck.rps requests a second). urls narrows the check to some of the page's links; a URL the page does not link is not requested.
tools.get: The outline of the views: headings, landmarks, links, images, forms, focus order, accessibility tree (Chromium) and custom selectors. shape merged (default) gives one row per entry with a cell per view and `only` naming the views it is visible in; shape views gives each view's own lists. sections picks the sections; findings are included with severity, element and view - every rule but the link check, those over the breakpoints (heading-differs, landmark-differs, interactive-differs) and the reading order among them. findingsOnly answers the views and findings without the lists.
tools.mark: Marks an outline entry in the views and scrolls it into view: targets lists per view a selector or an accessibility backendNodeId; clear removes every mark.
tools.reading_order: The reading order of the views: per view the headings and interactive elements whose place on the screen runs against the source order (reading-order, WCAG 1.3.2, both elements named, the other one's selector in data.other) and the focus jumping back against the visible order (focus-order-jump, WCAG 2.4.3); right to left where the page reads so, with outline.readingOrder.tolerancePx.
